course.description: A complete and deeply explained Java programming guide covering fundamentals, object-oriented programming, collections, multithreading, JDBC, Spring Boot, design patterns, JVM internals, microservices, testing, deployment, and enterprise development.

chapters.chapterDescription: This chapter explains Java basics, history, architecture, and how Java programs execute.

topics.description: Java was created by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems in 1995. Originally named Oak, it was designed for interactive television but became the language of the internet due to its 'Write Once, Run Anywhere' capability.

content.detailedExplanation: Java was designed for platform-independent programming. The motto of Java is Write Once Run Anywhere (WORA). Java became popular because compiled Java code can run on all operating systems using JVM.

topics.description: Java's popularity stems from its unique set of features like simplicity, platform independence, and built-in security, making it ideal for enterprise-level applications.

features.name: Simple
features.explanation: Java syntax is simple and easy to learn.

features.name: Object Oriented
features.explanation: Everything in Java is based on classes and objects.

features.name: Secure
features.explanation: Java provides runtime security and memory safety.

features.name: Portable
features.explanation: Compiled bytecode can run on multiple operating systems.

features.name: Multithreaded
features.explanation: Java supports concurrent execution of tasks.

features.name: Robust
features.explanation: Java handles memory automatically using Garbage Collection.

topics.description: These three components form the backbone of Java. The JDK is for development, JRE is for running apps, and JVM is the engine that actually executes the code.

JRE.description: Provides environment to run Java applications.

steps: Create Java file
Compile using javac
Run using java command

chapters.chapterDescription: Variables store data and data types define the kind of data.

topics.description: Primitive data types are the most basic data types available in Java. There are 8 types including byte, short, int, long, float, double, char, and boolean.
A variable is a container which holds the value while the Java program is executed. A variable is assigned with a data type.
Type casting is when you assign a value of one primitive data type to another type. It can be Widening (automatic) or Narrowing (manual).

implicitCasting.description: Widening Casting (automatically) - converting a smaller type to a larger type size.

example.code:
int x = 10;
double y = x;

explicitCasting.description: Narrowing Casting (manually) - converting a larger type to a smaller size type.

example.code:
double x = 10.5;
int y = (int)x;

topics.description: Used to perform basic mathematical operations like addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
Used to compare two values. They return a boolean result (true or false).
Used to determine the logic between variables or values (AND, OR, NOT).
Operators that need only one operand to perform any operation.
Used to assign values to variables, often combined with arithmetic operations.
The 'if' statement is the most basic control flow statement. It tells your program to execute a certain section of code only if a particular test evaluates to true.
The 'if-else' statement provides a secondary path of execution when an 'if' clause evaluates to false.
The 'switch' statement allows a variable to be tested for equality against a list of values. Each value is called a case.
Loops in Java are used to execute a set of instructions repeatedly until a particular condition is satisfied.

forLoop.description: Best used when the number of iterations is known in advance.

whileLoop.description: Best used when the number of iterations is not known in advance.

doWhileLoop.description: Guarantees that the code block will execute at least once.

topics.description: A linear list of elements of the same type stored in contiguous memory locations.
The process of visiting each element in the array exactly once, usually using a loop.
An array of arrays, commonly used to represent tables, matrices, or grids.
A method is a block of code which only runs when it is called. You can pass data, known as parameters, into a method.
With method overloading, multiple methods can have the same name with different parameters.
Recursion is the technique of making a function call itself. This technique provides a way to break complicated problems down into simple problems.
A class is a template for objects, and an object is an instance of a class. When the individual objects are created, they inherit all the variables and methods from the class.
A constructor in Java is a special method that is used to initialize objects. The constructor is called when an object of a class is created.
In Java, it is possible to inherit attributes and methods from one class to another. We group the inheritance concept into two categories: subclass and superclass.
The ability of an object to take on many forms. Java supports Compile-time (Overloading) and Runtime (Overriding) polymorphism.
Data abstraction is the process of hiding certain details and showing only essential information to the user. Abstraction can be achieved with either abstract classes or interfaces.
An interface is a completely 'abstract class' that is used to group related methods with empty bodies.
The meaning of Encapsulation, is to make sure that 'sensitive' data is hidden from users. To achieve this, you must declare class variables/attributes as private.
Java has a set of built-in methods that you can use on strings to manipulate text easily.
Mutable sequence of characters.

The 'try' statement allows you to define a block of code to be tested for errors while it is being executed. The 'catch' statement allows you to define a block of code to be executed, if an error occurs in the try block.
User-defined exceptions.
Resizable array implementation.
Doubly linked list.
Stores unique values.
Stores key-value pairs.

chapters.chapterDescription: Java's ability to run multiple threads simultaneously for high performance.

topics.description: Threads can be created either by extending the Thread class or by implementing the Runnable interface. The interface approach is generally preferred as it allows the class to inherit from other classes.
Synchronization in Java is the capability to control the access of multiple threads to any shared resource. It is used to prevent thread interference and consistency errors.

example.code: synchronized void deposit(int amount) { ... }

topics.description: Modern way to manage a pool of threads.
The java.io package contains nearly all the classes you might need to perform input and output (I/O) in Java. All these streams represent an input source and an output destination.
Converting an object into a byte stream to save to a file or send over network.

topics.description: The JVM consists of three main subsystems: Class Loader, Runtime Data Areas (Memory), and Execution Engine.
Automatic memory management that reclaims heap space used by objects that are no longer reachable.

chapters.chapterDescription: This chapter connects Java concepts with real coding tasks, debugging habits, interview preparation, and project building.

topics.description: Debugging means finding why the program is not working as expected. A Java developer should read the error message carefully, check the line number, understand the exception type, and test one change at a time.
steps: Read the complete compiler or runtime error message
Find the exact file name and line number
Check spelling, brackets, semicolons, imports, and data types
Print important variable values or use a debugger breakpoint
Fix one issue, run again, and confirm the output

explanation.printStatements: Temporary print statements help you verify the value before important logic.
explanation.condition: The if condition checks the value and chooses the correct block.

topics.description: Interviewers usually test whether you can explain concepts clearly with small examples. Do not memorize only definitions; understand the reason and usage.

features.name: Why is Java platform independent?
features.explanation: Java compiles source code into bytecode, and JVM runs that bytecode on different operating systems.

features.name: Difference between JDK, JRE, and JVM
features.explanation: JDK develops Java programs, JRE runs Java programs, and JVM executes bytecode.

features.name: Difference between overloading and overriding
features.explanation: Overloading happens in the same class with different parameters. Overriding happens in a child class with the same method signature.

features.name: Why use collections?
features.explanation: Collections store and process groups of objects more flexibly than fixed-size arrays.
